  <div class="tab-pane fade" id="nav-bhatta-murari-life" role="tabpanel">
  Bhaṭṭa Murāri is believed to have lived in the 9th century CE, and he was a Brāhmaṇa who belonged to the Maudgalya Gotra. It is believed that he lived on the banks of the Narmadā River in central India.<br>Bhaṭṭa Murāri is known for his literary works, which include poems, plays, and hymns. His most famous work is Anargharāghava, which is a retelling of the Rāmāyaṇa story. Anargharāghava is known for its poetic language and vivid descriptions of the characters and events in the story. His works are considered to be important contributions to Sanskrit literature and have been studied and admired for centuries.
  </div>
  <div class="tab-pane fade" id="nav-bhatta-murari-contribution" role="tabpanel">
  Bhaṭṭa Murāri’s contribution to Classical Sanskrit literature is significant. He was a prolific writer and composed works in various genres, including plays, poetry, and prose. His works are known for their linguistic beauty, rich imagery, and philosophical depth.<br><br>In addition to Anargharāghava, Bhaṭṭa Murāri is also known for his various other works. Bhaṭṭa Murāri’s writing style reflects a deep understanding of the Sanskrit literary tradition, as well as a creative and innovative approach to language and imagery. His works have influenced generations of Sanskrit writers and continue to be studied and admired for their literary and philosophical content.
  </div>
